summary: This is a facility asset inspection dashboard system from circa 2017-2018. The core business logic (logic.js) calculates risk levels for physical assets based on how overdue their inspections are, using a ratio of days-since-last-check to required check interval. Assets are classified as low/medium/high risk, with keyword scanning in condition notes forcing high risk if 'fail' appears. The jQuery dashboard (dashboard.js) fetches asset data via AJAX, processes it through the logic module, and renders a sortable/filterable HTML table with color-coded risk rows. A separate PowerShell script runs nightly via scheduled task to scan individual asset log files and generate a CSV summary report. The JS modules use callbacks despite being synchronous, maintain global state counters and caches, and the presentation layer tightly couples DOM manipulation with business logic.
risks: Global mutable state in logic.js (_cache and _riskCounter) will cause race conditions and stale data if processAssets is called multiple times or concurrently - each call mutates shared state without cleanup

Callback hell anti-pattern: getRisk uses callbacks despite being synchronous, and processAssets executes all getRisk callbacks immediately in a loop then synchronously sorts - the callback is misleading and suggests async behavior that doesn't exist

IIFE closure around asset in processAssets loop creates unnecessary function objects for every asset - this was needed in old ES5 to capture loop variables but indicates the author didn't understand the synchronous execution
No error handling: getRisk callback receives err parameter but never passes errors; dashboard.js alert() on AJAX failure provides no recovery mechanism or logging
daysBetween calculation uses Math.abs which hides data quality issues - if last_checked is in the future due to bad data entry, it will silently calculate wrong risk
Risk calculation keyword search uses indexOf instead of regex and only checks for 'fail' substring - will false-positive on 'failure-resistant', 'fail-safe', 'unfailing' etc.

Sorting happens after ALL assets are processed but out array is populated synchronously in loop order - the sort is working on complete data by accident of synchronous execution, would break if truly async
Module cache never invalidates - if same asset is processed twice with different data, cache returns stale risk level from first calculation
jQuery dashboard stores lastLoadedAssets in global scope - multiple dashboard instances on same page would conflict
String concatenation for HTML in renderTable creates XSS vulnerability - if asset.name or asset.category contain malicious HTML/script tags they'll execute
PowerShell script reads entire log file into memory for each asset then takes last line - will fail with large log files (>1GB per asset would cause out-of-memory)
PowerShell uses += to build results array - this creates a new array copy on each iteration, O(n²) performance that will timeout with thousands of assets
No error handling in PowerShell if log file is empty, malformed, or last line doesn't have expected comma-separated format - will write partial/corrupt CSV
PowerShell hardcodes absolute paths C:\AssetLogs and C:\Reports - not portable across environments or testable without modifying production directories

Date handling assumes ISO format strings but doesn't validate - new Date(asset.last_checked) will return Invalid Date for malformed input and Math.round(NaN) returns NaN, breaking risk calculation silently
No dependency version pinning - jQuery version unspecified, logic.js exported differently for browser vs Node (typeof module check), fragile cross-environment compatibility
js_modernization_plan: Create comprehensive test suite FIRST before any refactoring: unit tests for daysBetween with edge cases (same day, leap years, invalid dates), getRisk with all risk thresholds and keyword scenarios, processAssets with empty arrays and mixed risk levels. Capture current behavior including bugs as regression tests.

Extract pure risk calculation logic into standalone functions with no side effects: separate calculateDaysSince(lastChecked, now), calculateRiskRatio(days, interval), determineRiskLevel(ratio), hasFailureKeyword(notes). Remove global _cache and _riskCounter entirely.

Replace callback pattern with direct return values since everything is synchronous: getRisk should return {days, overdue, risk} object directly, processAssets should return processed array directly. This is a straightforward refactor since callbacks are never actually async.

Convert ES5 var/function syntax to ES6+ const/let/arrow functions and proper modules: use const for immutable values, let for loop counters, arrow functions to eliminate IIFE closures, proper export/import statements instead of conditional module.exports.

Add explicit input validation with meaningful errors: check asset object has required fields (id, last_checked, check_interval_days), validate date strings parse correctly, throw/return errors instead of silently producing NaN or undefined.

Replace string indexOf keyword search with configurable regex array: define RISK_KEYWORDS = [/\bfail(ed|ure)?\b/i, /\bbrok(en)?\b/i] with word boundaries to prevent false positives, make it easy to add new risk indicators.

Implement proper date handling with explicit timezone: use date-fns or Temporal API instead of native Date to handle ISO strings correctly, make 'now' an injectable parameter for testability instead of new Date() inside function.

Refactor processAssets to use map/sort chain: assets.map(asset => ({...asset, ...calculateRiskData(asset)})).sort((a,b) => RISK_ORDER[a.riskLevel] - RISK_ORDER[b.riskLevel]) - more declarative and eliminates manual loop/accumulator.
Create TypeScript interfaces or JSDoc types for Asset, RiskAssessment, ProcessedAsset to document expected shape and enable IDE autocomplete and basic type checking without full TS migration.

For dashboard.js, create a DashboardController class to encapsulate state (currentFilter, lastLoadedAssets) and methods (loadAssets, renderTable, applyFilter) - eliminates global variables and enables multiple instances.

Replace jQuery AJAX with fetch API and proper promise chain: fetch('/api/assets').then(r => r.json()).then(processAssets).then(renderTable).catch(handleError) - easier to test and debug, modern standard.

Replace jQuery DOM manipulation with template literals and safe HTML escaping: create escapeHtml(str) utility, use element.innerHTML with escaped values or createElement/textContent for dynamic data. Eliminates XSS without framework dependency.
Add loading states and error UI instead of alert(): show spinner during fetch, display friendly error message in dashboard area with retry button, log errors to monitoring service.

Extract renderTable row generation into separate function: createAssetRow(asset, rowClass) returns DocumentFragment or template element - more testable and enables virtual DOM diffing if needed later.

Make risk level ordering and CSS classes configurable: define RISK_CONFIG = {high: {order: 0, class: 'row-danger', label: 'HIGH'}, ...} object to centralize risk display logic and enable easy addition of new levels.
Add URL-based filter persistence: use URLSearchParams to read/write currentFilter to query string so filters survive page refresh and can be bookmarked/shared.
Implement proper module bundler setup (Vite/esbuild): create development workflow with hot reload, production build with minification, separate vendor chunks, source maps for debugging.

Consider framework adoption decision point: if this dashboard will grow significantly, create migration path to React/Vue/Svelte with component architecture; if staying simple, formalize vanilla JS component pattern with custom elements.
powershell_modernization_plan: Design modern cross-platform CLI tool specification: define command-line interface with --log-dir, --output-file, --format (csv|json|excel) flags, proper exit codes (0=success, 1=validation error, 2=IO error), structured error output to stderr, progress reporting to stdout.

Choose target platform and language: evaluate PowerShell Core 7+ (cross-platform, familiar to Windows ops), Python with Click/Typer (better error handling, richer ecosystem), or Node.js (shares ecosystem with dashboard) - recommend PowerShell Core to minimize ops team retraining.

Rewrite file reading with streaming/tail approach: use Get-Content -Tail 1 to read only last line instead of loading entire file into memory, add -ErrorAction Stop to catch missing/locked files, validate line format before parsing.

Replace array concatenation with ArrayList or pipeline accumulator: use System.Collections.Generic.List[PSObject] for O(1) append, or pipe Get-ChildItem directly to ForEach-Object to Select-Object to Export-Csv without intermediate collection.

Add comprehensive parameter validation: use [ValidateScript] to check log directory exists and is readable, validate output path is writable, add -WhatIf and -Confirm support for safety, implement [CmdletBinding()] for proper PowerShell cmdlet behavior.

Implement structured error handling with try/catch per file: wrap each log file processing in try block, catch specific exceptions (FileNotFoundException, UnauthorizedAccessException, FormatException), accumulate errors in separate collection, write error summary at end.

Add logging and observability: implement -Verbose output with detailed progress per file, -Debug for troubleshooting malformed lines, optionally write JSON log with execution metadata (runtime, files processed, errors) for monitoring integration.

Make CSV parsing configurable: add parameters for expected column count, delimiter character, date format validation, optional strict mode that fails on any malformed line vs. lenient mode that skips and logs.

Externalize configuration to JSON/YAML file: move hardcoded paths, expected log format, output columns to config file, add --config parameter to specify location, support environment variable substitution for paths.

Add unit tests using Pester 5: test ParseLogLine function with valid/invalid inputs, mock Get-ChildItem and Get-Content to test business logic without filesystem dependency, test error handling paths, use Test-ModuleManifest for manifest validation.

Implement idempotency and incremental processing: add option to track last-processed timestamp per log file, only process files modified since last run, store checkpoint state in JSON file, add --full flag to override and reprocess everything.

Create proper module structure: manifest file (.psd1) with version/author/dependencies, separate functions into public (Export-ModuleMember) and private helpers, dot-source pattern for file organization, support Install-Module distribution.

Add output format flexibility: support JSON output with full object graph (not just flattened CSV), Excel output using ImportExcel module with formatting/charts, HTML report option with embedded risk visualization.

Implement parallel processing for large deployments: use ForEach-Object -Parallel (PS7+) to process multiple log files concurrently with -ThrottleLimit for resource control, add progress bar with percentage complete across all files.

Create Docker container for scheduled execution: write Dockerfile with PowerShell Core, mount log directory and output directory as volumes, use cron or Kubernetes CronJob instead of Windows Task Scheduler for cloud portability.

Add integration with modern asset management API: instead of writing CSV, optionally POST results directly to centralized API endpoint, implement retry logic with exponential backoff, support batch upload to handle thousands of assets efficiently.

Implement migration path from old scheduled task: create installation script that backs up existing task, migrates configuration to new format, sets up new scheduled task/cron job, validates output matches old script for parallel run period.

Add data quality validation and alerting: check for assets with no recent log entries, detect log files that haven't been updated in X days (dead sensors), validate parsed dates are reasonable (not year 1900 or future), send alerts for anomalies via webhook/email.
